deep.reconstruction:
Context. In cote 151 Grothendieck encodes a stratified space (or stratified topos) with strata indexed by a poset I as gluing data.
- For each stratum i there is the open stratum X_i^*.
- For each pair i ≤ j there is a 'tubular' piece V_{i,j}, morally a neighbourhood of X_i^*, receiving X_i^* → V_{i,j}.
- There is also a 'deleted' piece V_{i,j}^* (the part of that neighbourhood lying in the stratum j, a link-type object). It maps both into V_{i,j} and to X_j^*.

On the previous page he drew the resulting zig-zag diagrams X_i^* → V_{i,j} ← V_{i,j}^* → X_j^*. For a totally ordered I = {0 < 1 < … < n} this gives a staircase (20). For a span or cospan I it gives (21) and (22).

This page. He supposes I carries an integer-valued 'dimension' function d: I → Z, so that I = ⊔_m I_m (23). He remarks that a dual presentation using a codimension-type function would also work. The required condition (24) is: for i ≤ j, d(j) = d(i)+1 ⇔ j is an immediate successor of i. Thus d is a rank function making I a graded poset.

He then aggregates the strata by dimension (25):
- X_m^* = ⊔_{i∈I_m} X_i^*;
- V_{m,m+1} = ⊔ V_{i,j} over pairs i ≤ j with d(i) = m and d(j) = m+1;
- V^*_{m,m+1} is defined similarly.

This yields for each m a diagram (Diag)_m (26): X_m^* → V_{m,m+1} ← V^*_{m,m+1} → X^*_{m+1}. These fit together into a single staircase diagram 'like (20) in principle'. That is, the gluing data for an arbitrary graded stratification is put in the same linear shape as for a totally ordered (flag-like) stratification.

The last (heavily corrected) lines say this will be written in simplified form, indexed by d(I) (finite, or a filtrant subset of Z). Vertices of the diagram corresponding to empty pieces may be occupied by empty spaces.

Purpose: reduce the combinatorics of the poset of strata to a Z-indexed chain. This is a dévissage of the stratified object by dimension, analogous to the skeletal filtration of a CW complex. The space should then be recovered as an iterated pushout / homotopy colimit of this chain.
errors: Condition (24) alone does not force d to be strictly monotone on non-comparable-to-adjacent pairs. One needs i < j ⇒ d(i) < d(j) (a genuine rank function, with every maximal chain between i and j of length d(j) − d(i)) for the aggregation to behave as intended.

The aggregated diagram (25)–(26) only keeps the V_{i,j} with d(j) = d(i)+1. The tubular data for non-adjacent pairs i < j (d(j) − d(i) ≥ 2), present in the full diagram, are discarded. These are needed in general (cf. the higher 'corner' compatibilities in Mather/Thom control data or in exit-path categories), so the simplified chain loses information unless one argues that those data are determined by the adjacent ones. The page does not address this.

Taking disjoint unions of the V_{i,j} over all pairs with fixed dimensions makes the map X_m^* → V_{m,m+1} non-injective in general: one X_i^* maps to several V_{i,j}. So V_{m,m+1} is not a neighbourhood of X_m^*. The aggregated diagram is a formal recombination, not a geometric neighbourhood decomposition.

ideas.what: Encoding a stratified space by open strata X_i^*, neighbourhoods V_{ij} and deleted neighbourhoods/links V_{ij}^* in a zig-zag diagram over the poset of strata
ideas.modern_name: homotopy links / gluing data of a stratified space; exit-path (∞-)category description; tubular (Mather/Thom) control data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather (control data, 1970); Quinn (homotopy links, 1988); MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (exit paths, 2000s); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (dévissage of stratified structures, tubular neighbourhoods, 'tame topology') — only in outline

ideas.what: Grading the poset of strata by a dimension (or codimension) function with the cover condition, and aggregating strata of equal dimension to reduce the gluing diagram to a Z-indexed staircase
ideas.modern_name: graded (ranked) poset of strata; filtration by dimension / skeletal dévissage
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Whitney/Thom stratifications indexed by dimension; Goresky–MacPherson filtered spaces)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working page in Grothendieck's program for stratified topoi. It regroups strata by dimension to linearize gluing diagrams. The ideas match his Esquisse outline and are standard in later stratified-homotopy literature (filtered spaces, homotopy links, exit paths). Nothing here is a finished result or a new connection, and the simplification even drops the non-adjacent gluing data.
transcription_corrections: Line after (23): '(en an[?] une présentation…' should read '(on aurait une présentation en quelque sorte duale avec une fonction type codimension)'.
'satisfaisant la condition' should read 'satisfaisant à la condition'.
In (24) Grothendieck first wrote 'i,j ∈ I_d' and crossed out the subscript; the final text is 'si i,j ∈ I, i ≤ j, alors d(j)=d(i)+1 ⇔ j succ. de i'.
'Posons alors, pour m,n ∈ Z' is more likely 'Posons donc, pour m,n ∈ Z' (n written over something).
In (25) the second line was first written V^*_{m,m+1} with the star crossed out, so it is V_{m,m+1} without star. The first line has X_m^* written over another index.
'on trouve [?] des diagrammes' is probably 'on trouve ainsi les diagrammes' (reading uncertain).
's'insérant dans un diagramme commun [en] principe' should read 's'insérant dans un diagramme comme (20) en principe'; the '(20)' is part of a struck/inserted phrase.

Final lines read roughly: '…mais qu'on écrira sous forme simplifiée (indexée par d(I) ⊂ Z, fini ou filtrant), et en n'écrivant pas les parties du diagramme correspondant à des sommets occupés par des espaces vides' (partly uncertain).
